chose: single OpenRouter gateway entry in lib/ai/provider.ts, default model mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501
over: keeping openai-compatible and just repointing baseURL at openrouter.ai
because: OpenRouter fronts every vendor behind one key and base URL, so changing WHICH model runs becomes an LLM_ENRICHMENT_MODEL edit rather than a new registry entry, dependency and secret; the dedicated provider also carries OpenRouter-only routing options the generic openai-compatible shim cannot express. @ai-sdk/openai-compatible dropped from services/pipeline deps — nothing else imported it.

chose: kept ResolvedProvider.providerOptions as the per-entry call-options seam, empty for openrouter
over: deleting the field now that no entry populates it
because: instance count is 0 today, but the seam is one line ({}) and OpenRouter's own knobs (reasoning, models fallback routing, user) are live candidates; deleting it would churn ResolvedProvider, queues/recipe-enrichment/index.ts and capture.test.ts for no user-visible gain. Re-run: grep -rn providerOptions services/pipeline/src

chose: left docs/plans/* and .coherence/* moonshot references in place
because: they are dated historical records of what was decided and measured at the time (2026-08-26/27/28 llm-enrichment plans + results); rewriting them would fabricate a history in which Moonshot was never chosen. Live config, code and AGENTS.md were swapped instead.

chose: mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501 returns a different diet verdict for the SAME recipe across identical forced re-runs: 'Black Bean and Sweet Potato Chili' (olive oil, onion, sweet potato, jalapeno, garlic, spices, tomatoes, vegetable broth, black beans) got diet/vegan=excluded on two runs and diet/vegan=likely on a third, with vegetarian/dairy_free/pescatarian flipping alongside
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
ordinary sampling noise at the AI SDK default temperature, which generateText in queues/recipe-enrichment/index.ts never pins
the model genuinely misreads the prompt's 'excluded' verdict as 'this diet applies', so the label is inverted whenever it fires
the smaller model is simply weaker than kimi-k2 on this dimension and the rules classifier is not covering for it — the chili has NO rules@ diet rows at all, while the ham salad does
discriminatedBy: set temperature: 0 on the generateText call and force-re-run the same recipe 5x: stable-and-correct implicates temperature, stable-and-wrong implicates prompt comprehension, still-flapping implicates model capacity

chose: mistralai/mistral-small-2603 emitted ZERO diet labels on all 3 forced runs of the vegan 'Black Bean and Sweet Potato Chili', where mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501 flapped between vegan=likely (correct) and vegan=excluded (wrong). Control: on 'Classic Ham Salad' 2603 DID emit diet/dairy_free=excluded and diet/gluten_free=excluded, both correct — so it emits diets when it judges them non-default, it just declines to affirm 'likely'
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes

2603 reads the prompt's 'Emit ONLY non-default judgments' more literally and treats an affirmative diet fit as a default it may omit — conservative but uninformative, which suits the safety-asymmetric merge better than 2501's wrong excluded
2603 is simply unwilling to affirm diet fit without an explicit signal, and would stay silent even if the prompt asked for it
discriminatedBy: re-run both models on 5 unambiguously vegan recipes with a prompt variant that explicitly requests an affirmative verdict when a diet clearly fits; if 2603 then emits vegan=likely the omission is prompt-driven, if it stays silent it is model behavior
